title: A model for accurate quantification of CRISPR effects in pooled FACS screens
model: Primary human CD4+ T cells (3 donors), ~1,350-gene transcription-factor knockout library, CD25 (IL2RA) FACS sort into 4 bins at low/high coverage and MOI
contrast: Highest vs lowest CD25 bin (Q4 vs Q1), low-coverage high-MOI screen, paired by donor (3 vs 3); high-coverage low-MOI screen as second analysis
paper_method: Waterbear (Bayesian random-effects model over all four bins); MAGeCK and MAUDE for comparison
paper_calls: Low-coverage high-MOI screen: Waterbear 79/1,350 genes (24 of 26 previously validated IL2RA regulators), MAGeCK 31 (17/26), MAUDE 406 (25/26); no gene table published
barcs_calls: 82 genes at FDR 0.10 (45 up, 37 down in CD25-high); 70 against the control null centred on the targeting guides. High-coverage low-MOI screen: 107 genes
named_hits: 13/14 at FDR 0.10; ranks: MED12 #1, MYB #2, HIVEP2 #3, STAT5B #4, CBFB #5, IL2RA #6, KLF2 #7, TNFAIP3 #9, FOXK1 #10, ZNF217 #13, STAT5A #14, ATXN7L3 #23, JAK3 #37; IRF4 #131 (FDR 0.25)
verdict: Using only the outer two of four bins, BARCS recovers the paper's result: the cheap low-coverage, high-MOI screen still finds the validated IL2RA regulators (13 of 14 named, IRF4 missed), and it calls about as many genes (82) as Waterbear (79), well above MAGeCK's 31.
